declared_purpose: Manage Tencent Meeting meetings, invitations, attendance and live controls; retrieve recordings, transcripts and AI minutes; request recording access; support version maintenance and consented feedback. Directory lookup is restricted to immediately supporting explicit invitations or calls. Sources: SKILL.md lines 3, 19–27, 55–67 and 98–107.

data_operations.operation: Read local configuration and authentication credential
data_operations.source: CLI arguments, packaged config.json and TENCENT_MEETING_TOKEN
data_operations.data_scope: Requested method and arguments, service URL, skill version and authentication token
data_operations.condition: After argument validation, including calls ultimately handled entirely locally. A missing token prevents local preference calls too.

data_operations.data_scope: OS family and release/build or distribution version. Agent and model identifiers come from supplied _client_info, rather than local detection.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Request arguments in process memory; subsequently the MCP endpoint on remote calls
data_operations.condition: Only tools/call requests already containing a valid _client_info object trigger detection. The script overwrites its os field. This also happens before local-tool interception. Documentation requires the object on every tool call, while code permits its absence.

data_operations.operation: Transmit authenticated remote requests and receive results
data_operations.data_scope: Entire supplied parameters, including business inputs and _client_info when present; authentication token and skill version in headers
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: https://mcp.meeting.tencent.com/mcp/wemeet-open/v1; responses return to the CLI caller
data_operations.condition: Every request except the two intercepted local preference tools, including tools/list. The proxy performs no field minimization or redaction. Remote tool schemas are referenced but not packaged.

data_operations.source: User instructions and earlier meeting-tool responses
data_operations.data_scope: Meeting identifiers, subjects, schedules, passwords/settings, invitation identifiers, search terms and meeting-list results
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent Meeting MCP service; returned information goes to the caller and documented user-facing response
data_operations.condition: Creation, modification, cancellation or requested lookup. Modification and cancellation require prior display and confirmation. Meeting-code conversion and time resolution are explicitly prescribed. Cancellation is a business-state operation; source does not establish record erasure.

data_operations.operation: Resolve enterprise members for invitations or calls
data_operations.source: User-provided name, phone numbers, email addresses and optional department/job filters
data_operations.data_scope: Lookup identifiers sent to the service; open_id returned for action parameters. A unique name match is documented to return only open_id; multiple candidates can include names, jobs and departments.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent Meeting directory tools; identifiers then pass to meeting-action tools. Candidate labels may be shown to the requesting user.
data_operations.condition: An explicit current-turn invitation or call must immediately use the result. General personnel queries and directory lookup for kicking are prohibited. Multiple candidates require user selection. Phone/email echoes must be masked; cross-session retention of phone/email/open_id is prohibited by policy.

data_operations.operation: Read membership and change invitation or live participation state
data_operations.source: Meeting membership responses and user-selected targets
data_operations.data_scope: Invitee, participant and waiting-room lists; open_id/ms_open_id, device instanceid, departure status, selected targets and allow_rejoin
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent Meeting MCP service; designated members receive calls on the call path
data_operations.condition: Requested membership management. Kicking requires participant retrieval, local filtering of departed records, deduplication and device-based identifier routing. Calling and kicking require confirmation. Invitation removal/replacement requires current-list review. These operations do not establish deletion of personal records.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve and display complete post-change invitation information
data_operations.source: Invitation mutation response, subsequent get_meeting_invitees and, if needed, get_meeting
data_operations.data_scope: Meeting subject, time, code, join URL and entire final invitee roster using directory names; trace identifiers
data_operations.condition: The dedicated invitation-change template explicitly requires these fields after add/remove/replace, including another roster lookup. Internal identifiers remain hidden unless explicitly requested.

data_operations.source: Meeting attendance and interaction statistics held by the service
data_operations.data_scope: Complete requested participation statistics, cumulative attendance duration, interaction measures, job identifier and download URL
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent Meeting export service; artifact storage location is unspecified; download URL returns to the caller
data_operations.condition: For full statistics or attendance analysis, rather than ordinary participant viewing. Job status is polled. The documented URL validity is two hours; artifact retention is not specified. Packaged code does not download the artifact.

data_operations.operation: Retrieve and search recordings, transcripts and generated minutes
data_operations.source: Tencent Meeting recording and minutes tools
data_operations.data_scope: Meeting/recording identifiers, search terms and time filters; recording metadata and URLs; transcript text, speakers and timestamps; AI overviews, points, tasks and rolling summaries
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent Meeting MCP service for queries; results return to the caller and requested user-facing output
data_operations.condition: Route depends on requested content, available permissions and recording readiness. Generated summaries are retrieved products, not evidence of local AI generation. Rolling-minute retrieval explicitly fetches every page and aggregates the results. Yuanbao summaries may differ by the requester's attendance interval.

data_operations.operation: Preview and submit a recording-access application
data_operations.data_scope: Recording identifier, meeting title, recording owner, applicant, application description and approval identifiers/status/link
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: MCP service; preview shown to the requester; confirmed application directed to the recording owner
data_operations.condition: Explicit access request or recording-permission failure. Preview may begin automatically, but commit requires the requester to see the preview and explicitly agree. Preview expiry is documented; application retention is unknown.

data_operations.source: Encountered tool problem or suggestion and any necessary user-supplied details
data_operations.data_scope: Category, intended task, tool name, error code and necessary diagnostic descriptions, with private information redacted
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: submit_feedback at the Tencent Meeting MCP endpoint; feedback identifier returns to the requester
data_operations.condition: Problems mandate offering feedback, but the detailed rules require explicit consent before transmission. Submitted fields must match the redacted preview; the same issue is reported once per conversation. Backend retention is unspecified.

data_operations.operation: Return tool content and errors through stdout
data_operations.source: Local or remote tool response and caught exceptions
data_operations.data_scope: Text content, fallback JSON or error messages. Documentation additionally requires user-visible trace identifiers and contextual error guidance.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI caller through stdout; filesystem-operation warnings use stderr
data_operations.condition: On tool completion or failure. The script does not redact response text. A normal return to the caller is not evidence of additional external disclosure or durable logging; user-facing privacy handling is prescribed separately.

data_operations.operation: Persist local update preferences and compute prompt decisions
data_operations.source: User-selected update action, latest-version input, existing local state and local clock
data_operations.data_scope: Update/auto-upgrade flags; snoozed version, repetition level and timestamp; derived deadline, remaining time and prompt decision
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: ~/.tencent-meeting-mcp/update-state.json; selected state and derived decision return to the caller
data_operations.condition: The two preference tools execute locally without MCP forwarding. Writes maintain mutually exclusive preference states. Repeated snoozes increase the duration. Reads merge existing state keys; writes serialize the resulting state.

data_operations.operation: Define additional persistence and metadata-clearing helpers
data_operations.source: Arguments to save_last_check and mark_just_upgraded; existing update state
data_operations.data_scope: Entire supplied check_result with timestamp, previous version, and snooze/upgrade-marker fields
data_operations.condition: Only if these helpers are invoked; no packaged caller invokes them. clear_after_upgrade writes null to two fields and retains the file and other fields. It is not file deletion or general history erasure.

data_operations.operation: Request version information and prescribe installation
data_operations.source: Server version hints and user update preferences
data_operations.data_scope: Current version, optional client metadata, local preference decisions and a remotely returned installation address
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Tencent Meeting MCP endpoint for check_skill_version; installer destinations and storage are unresolved
data_operations.condition: Version-related triggers or an approved update. Automatic installation requires prior auto-upgrade authorization. Documentation prescribes installation, but no installer or dedicated version-tool implementation is supplied.

potential_excess.data_scope: Exact OS release/build or Linux distribution version
potential_excess.condition: A remote tools/call supplies _client_info; documentation requests it for every tool call.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The entry requires an OS/agent/model environment identifier. Including precise OS version information is an implementation choice; no meeting-function dependency on that precision is supplied.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Execute the authenticated meeting operation and retain any genuinely required client-environment fields.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Send OS family by default; collect precise release/build only for a diagnostic need. This narrows data within an existing request.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Verify the remote schema accepts the coarser value; preserve required field names and business arguments.

potential_excess.data_scope: Authentication token and, when supplied, derived OS details for local preference calls
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI process memory only; these local calls do not transmit them to MCP
potential_excess.condition: get_skill_update_preference or set_skill_update_preference passes through generic bootstrap before local dispatch.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These tools only read or change device-local update preferences. Credential acquisition and client detection precede routing but are unused by their handlers.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Validate the local action, access the preference file and return the result.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Dispatch recognized local tools before token/configuration requirements and client-environment enrichment. Remove these redundant local reads without changing remote authentication.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep local argument validation and preference semantics; retain credential checks for remote requests.

potential_excess.data_scope: Entire existing invitee roster before a pure additive change
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: get_meeting_invitees response from Tencent Meeting to the caller
potential_excess.condition: Scenario 11 retrieves the current roster before every change, including add; the required final report separately obtains the updated roster.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Current-list review is explicitly necessary for removal/replacement confirmation. The unconditional pre-add read is an additional prescribed action.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Confirm the members being added, perform the addition and obtain the final roster required by the output contract.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Skip the pre-add roster request when target identifiers are already resolved and no existing-state decision requires it. Retain post-change verification. This removes a redundant request rather than trimming its response.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep current-list retrieval for removal/replacement, ambiguous changes, or an explicit request to inspect the existing roster.

potential_excess.data_scope: Mandatory directory real names for the complete final invitee roster
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Requesting user's conversation after an invitation change
potential_excess.condition: The dedicated success template requires directory names and prohibits nickname-style alternatives, including for unchanged invitees.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: This is an explicit presentation requirement. It increases identifying precision beyond the general nickname-first rule and the purpose of confirming a membership change.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Identify the final invited members accurately and report the completed change.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Revise the real-name requirement to allow unambiguous nicknames or user-approved labels while retaining the complete roster required by the template. This narrows user-visible data rather than removing the roster-verification operation.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Use sufficient identifying detail for ambiguous members and explicit real-name requests; preserve the full-list output and removal/replacement confirmations.

unknowns: Remote schemas and implementations are absent. Exact request requirements, response fields, authorization enforcement, backend retention, onward transfers and deletion cannot be established.
The host agent's execution is not supplied. Consent, directory-intent restrictions, feedback redaction and user-facing masking are documented rules rather than enforced proxy checks.

Recording URLs, approval links and export downloads are returned references. Their destinations, access controls and subsequent retrieval behavior are not established; a two-hour export URL lifetime does not establish artifact deletion.

Version installation behavior and installer source are absent. No packaged callers invoke save_last_check, mark_just_upgraded or clear_after_upgrade, so their use in an actual update remains unresolved.

Caller-side logging, conversation retention and persistence of ordinary stdout/tool results are unspecified. The directory retention prohibition does not establish deletion from host context or remote systems.
Whether coarser client metadata is accepted remains unresolved because the remote tool schemas are not supplied.
